summary: Refactor: trim, extend, split, arc extend, mirror, the linear pattern's omitted occurrences and offset now decide what happens to each sketch relation by one rule, declared on each relation kind in the relation registry, in place of each operation's own handling. An edit is described once as a map from old points and curves to new ones, each new piece with the span of the old curve it covers and whether it runs the same way or reversed. Each relation then gets exactly one outcome: kept, replaced on the new operands, removed with a reason, or blocked, which a trim asks you to confirm and the other edits refuse until the relation is removed. A relation kind declares a role for each operand: a point follows its point while it survives; a carrier, such as a line's direction, a radius or a point held on a curve, follows the piece that keeps the curve's identity, which shares that support; an extent, such as Equal length, Midpoint, a reference length or a curve Symmetric, follows only while the edit keeps the whole interval; a joint, such as a Tangent joint or a corner, follows the piece that still has that end; an angle ray follows the end it points toward. The origin and the H and V axes are never remapped. Routing goes by curve capabilities (interval, reverse, carrier), read through one curve traits reader (ends, centre, straight), not by line, arc or circle. Mirror and offset gain a copy with relations mode for agents, copyRelations, which copies the relations internal to the copied set onto the copy by the same rule; it is part of their shared request, so a region proposal previews exactly what the edit commits. With the same flag, creating or regrowing a sketch linear pattern copies the seed circle's reference dimensions onto each occurrence it adds, as a translation by the same rule, while the seed's driving relations keep driving every occurrence through the pattern. Profile copy has no copy mode, and circular patterns are body features with no sketch relations. Recorded outcomes for every existing trim, extend, split and arc extend case are compared before and after: 33 calls differ, each listed with its reason in the parity record, where the old handling was inconsistent between operations. (1) Extend now keeps relations, fixed coordinates and expressions on an old end that another edge still uses, as trim already did, instead of refusing them (12 calls), including a horizontal relation on a point pair two lines share (1) and a radius on a neighbouring arc (1). (2) Extend now carries a line angle's ray to the new end, as trim already did (5). (3) A reference length of a whole line is now blocked when trim, extend or split changes the line, as Equal length and Midpoint already were, instead of being kept with a new meaning (6). (4) Split now keeps relations on the edge's support (radius, parallel, point on circle) and a Tangent joint at the end the kept piece still holds, instead of refusing every relation on the edge (6), and one recorded case now splits and reports the sketch's existing unsolved residual (1). (5) Extend now refuses only a corner at the moved end, not a corner at the line's other end (1).
warning: Not breaking for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, controller output or CAD files. Some trims, extends and splits now give a different result, and each difference is deliberate. Extend and split accept some edits they used to refuse. A trim that changes a line's length now also asks you to confirm removing a reference length of that line. Extend and split refuse that change until the reference length is removed. Agents keep the same reply and error shapes; mirror-sketch-geometry, offset-sketch-loop, their proposal.mirror and proposal.offset region previews, and set-sketch-relation for a linear-pattern owner gain an optional copyRelations flag that is off by default; set-sketch-relation rejects it with invalid-edit on any other relation. A new linear-pattern owner now reserves its own id, so an owner id that an occurrence or a copied relation would reuse rejects with invalid-sketch-pattern instead of duplicate-sketch-id; either way nothing is applied.

checklist.schema: No schema change. The sketch graph, relation kinds, CAD document and save envelope, UPID, post schema and engine API are unchanged. Saved sketches open and save byte for byte as before. The relation definitions gain a remap rule in code only; nothing new is stored.
checklist.events: No execution event, input-version or cancellation change. Trim confirmations still list removedRelationIds and reject a mismatch with unconfirmed-sketch-trim-removals; extend and split refusals keep dependent-sketch-extend and dependent-sketch-split with the same bounded relation and point details. They now come from the blocked outcomes of the shared rule.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change. WebMCP keeps 49 CAD tools and 51,178 of 51,200 discovery bytes, measured: copyRelations is an optional boolean in the shared mirror and offset request schemas, which the edits and the proposal.mirror and proposal.offset arms of the region tools all validate, and on set-sketch-relation for a linear-pattern owner. The region tools register a compact proposal envelope and cad_describe_edits reads the edit contracts on demand, so discovery is unchanged. Reply shapes are unchanged. The public agent guide describes the new split, extend and trim outcomes and both copy modes.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Nothing is migrated or rewritten.
checklist.verification: The new pure-domain remap suite covers a split, a reversed piece flipping a point-to-line side and keeping a ray and both kinds of Symmetric, a full circle trimmed into an arc over the phase seam, an arc over 180 degrees, a point that leaves, a renamed point, a pattern seed, axes and the origin named by the edit, construction geometry, a split at a Coincident end, a trim exactly at an existing end and at a tangent contact, mirror copies about a graph line and about the V axis, an offset copy of a rectangle, a stand-in curve kind routed only by the traits an edit gives, and the reference dimensions a pattern occurrence copies. The parity suite replays every recorded trim, extend, split, arc extend, mirror, offset, profile copy and pattern reconcile call against its recorded outcome, allowing only the 33 listed differences. A visit-counting suite on a 2,002-relation sketch shows a warm remap, trim and extend make no point identity scan and read only the touched relation's definition. Mirror and offset with copyRelations commit what their region proposal previews, and a driving radius on a pattern seed still drives every occurrence after the seed's references are copied. Full Vitest passes (635 files, 7,379 tests); build, documentation check, lint and ui:check pass; each of the brief's five mutations and eleven more on the round 1 additions makes at least one test fail; a trim on a 2,003-relation sketch takes a median 60.93 ms against 61.97 ms on main over five alternating pairs; the trim, circle trim, arc extend, constraints (line trim, extend and split), mirror copy, linear pattern, offset, profile copy and relation glyph specs each pass alone. Since review round 1: copyRelations moved into the shared mirror and offset request schemas so preview and commit take one request; the sketch linear pattern copies seed reference dimensions behind the same flag, with distinct drop reasons; point identities are cached per accepted graph and shared by the remapper, trim and extend; curves are read through one traits reader. Since review round 2: a new pattern owner reserves its own id before its occurrence and copied relation ids are checked, with a regression for a copied reference, a circle and a centre that would reuse it.

publicNotes.summary: Trim, split, extend and mirror copy treat sketch relations by one rule.
changes: Split keeps relations on the edge's supporting line or circle, such as Parallel, a radius or a point held on the edge, on the piece that keeps the edge's identity, and keeps a Tangent joint at the end that piece still has. Equal length, Midpoint, a reference length and Symmetric curves on the edge still have to be removed first.
Extend keeps an old end that another edge still uses together with its relations, fixed coordinates and expressions, as Trim already did, and moves an angle at the extended end along with it.
Extend refuses only a fillet or chamfer at the end it moves, not one at the line's other end.
A reference length of a whole line is no longer kept when Trim, Split or Extend changes the line's length. Trim lists it for removal, and Split and Extend ask you to remove it first.

Agents can ask a mirror copy or an offset to carry the copied geometry's own relations onto the copy, and a sketch linear pattern to copy the seed circle's reference dimensions onto each copy it adds.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, controller output and CAD files are unchanged. Agent tools keep their reply shapes and gain one optional flag.
publicNotes.action: No action needed. If a trim now asks to remove a reference length, confirm it or remove the reference first.
